court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Mrs. Bharti Bhausaheb Aher vs Mr. Bhausaheb Kautik Aher
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnized on 21.2.1999. A son was born out of wedlock in 2000. After 11 years of marriage, the respondent-husband filed a Hindu Marriage Petition for divorce praying for a decree of divorce under section 13 (1) (ia) & (ib) and section 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A decree obtained by playing a fraud on the Court is null and void.
legal_principles.held: It is thus contended that the decree was obtained by playing a fraud on the Court and is accordingly null and void.

legal_principles.principle: A court should examine whether the consent terms are real or not.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that the Family Court ought to have examined whether the consent terms dated 12.6.2015 were at all the real terms of settlement between the parties.

outcome.final_order: The marriage was dissolved by decree of divorce by mutual consent u/s 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Respondent shall comply with consent terms at Exh.22. Consent terms at Exh 22 shall form part of the decree.
